items.title: Where does it fit, not which is best
items.body: Whittemore's frame for new models is a slot in a stack, and that suits an AI scribe or summarising tool in general practice. One model may write a better letter while another is safer at coding or data tasks. Ask a supplier which model sits underneath, whether it can change, and what evidence exists from UK primary care notes. Zitron would add that a strong demo says little about reliability or cost.

items.title: Consumer chatbots and health claims
items.body: Character AI is seeking bankruptcy protection partly over lawsuits about self-harm and chatbots posing as doctors. Patients are already using general chatbots for symptoms, so expect more consultations that begin with what a bot said. Ask what they were told, check it, and record it. Both positions agree these products need ordinary accountability, though they disagree on whether the business can last.

items.title: Agents, banks and liability
items.body: JPMorgan will not let outside agents act on customer accounts, and will not refund losses caused by one. The NHS version is any tool that acts on records or books and prescribes on a clinician's behalf. Check who carries liability before a practice lets an agent act, and keep a named clinical safety officer and hazard log under DCB0160. Little else in this edition bears directly on the NHS.
